why: Supplied live measurement (coordinator, not re-run by me): BackupService.create() produced a 28,235-byte custom dump and BackupService.restore() into a separate empty DB restored 3 facts. I reproduced the underlying pg_dump --format=custom / pg_restore --clean --if-exists round trip on pgvector/pgvector:pg16: 3 rows inserted, 2,615-byte custom dump, 3 rows restored into cortex_restore, and a same-DB --clean restore returned 3 rows. The CLI itself was not run against a live DB; its wiring is covered by 10 mocked tests in tests/unit/test_cli_backup.py. Caveat: both CLI commands call the composed get_settings() unconditionally, so they need LLM_API_KEY even with --db-url/--out (reproduced; see STD-2).

The dump call on line 73 runs before the apply loop on line 75, so the archive is the pre-migration schema plus the just-created schema_migrations table. Supplied live boot (coordinator): a fresh DB with the cortex-test image took a 1,824-byte pre-migration dump, then applied all migrations; the post-boot schema had 12 public tables. The exact pre-migration dump was not restored in that measurement; the AC-1 round trip exercises the same custom-format restore path. The unit test pins that a dump is taken when pending and none when not, but not the dump-before-apply ordering (see AC-6).

create() calls self._prune(keep=final) after os.replace, and _prune skips the keep path, so the just-created file is never deleted even if it falls outside the newest N. Tests: test_keeps_the_newest_n_and_the_just_created_file (retention=2, four creates, newest two remain), test_zero_retention_keeps_everything, test_delete_errors_are_logged_not_fatal. Ran: uv run pytest tests/config/test_safety.py tests/safety tests/unit/test_cli_backup.py tests/unit/test_migrations_backup.py -q -> 55 passed.

The password travels only in PGPASSWORD (backup.py:181); the URL passed to pg_dump/pg_restore is sanitize_database_url (backup.py:222/240); pg_dump/pg_restore stderr is redacted before it reaches BackupError. CLI output prints only path/size and the confirmation uses sanitize_database_url (cli.py:398-399). Tests: test_reason_is_logged_without_the_url, test_dump_uses_the_private_url_and_pgpassword_env, test_failure_is_an_error_without_the_password, test_confirmation_prompt_shows_the_sanitized_database_url; all in the 55-passed run. Residual advisory: a password supplied as a query parameter (?password=...) would survive sanitize_database_url; the repo's userinfo format does not.

quote: "database is in use; stop the app or pass --force"
why: restore() opens one asyncpg connection, counts pg_stat_activity rows with datname = current_database() and pid <> pg_backend_pid(), and raises before pg_restore when the count is nonzero; the check connection is closed in finally. The CLI confirms by default (typer.confirm, abort=True); --yes skips only the prompt; --force skips only the in-use check. Tests cover refuse, force, no-other-connection, close-on-error, and the CLI prompt/yes/no/force paths. Live check I ran on pgvector/pgvector:pg16 with the exact query: 0 with only the checking session, 1 with a second pg_sleep session. Semantics notes: the count includes background/autovacuum workers (no backend_type filter) and any idle session, and it is a pre-flight check (TOCTOU); --force while the app is still connected can make --clean block or fail on locks. None violates the documented 'any connection other than the check itself'.

Ran uv run pytest tests/config/test_safety.py tests/safety tests/unit/test_cli_backup.py tests/unit/test_migrations_backup.py -q -> 55 passed; canonical suite uv run pytest tests/config tests/safety tests/unit tests/learning tests/memory tests/eval tests/validation -q -> 1429 passed, 28 skipped. Coverage caveats: the transport tests use FakePgClient/RecordingRunner, so no test executes a real pg_dump/pg_restore or restores a real pre-migration dump; the migration test asserts a backup was taken when pending but not that it preceded the apply (a mutant moving _pre_migration_backup after the loop would stay green); the CLI tests monkeypatch get_settings, so the LLM_API_KEY prerequisite is untested.

The external-store half matches the contract (host ~/.local/share/cortex, bind-mounted at /var/lib/cortex/safety, one-shot safety-store init, 0600 dumps). But making the cortex service non-root without completing the ownership init breaks an existing write: the same service mounts mosquitto_config:/mosquitto/config:rw (docker-compose.yml:85) and sets MQTT_PASSWD_PATH=/mosquitto/config/passwd.conf (docker-compose.yml:76), which src/cortex/api/routes/minions.py:289 writes. The mosquitto image's /mosquitto/config is drwxr-xr-x mosquitto:mosquitto (uid/gid 1883) and its entrypoint chowns only /mosquitto/data; I ran docker run --rm --user 1000:1000 --entrypoint sh eclipse-mosquitto:2 -c 'touch /mosquitto/config/passwd.conf' -> Permission denied (exit 1). Minion MQTT credential creation/revocation therefore returns 500 in the default compose deployment. The one-shot init must cover that volume (or the app must get the right group). Secondary advisories: the store root is 0755 (observed on ~/.local/share/cortex; _ensure_dir chmods only backups at src/cortex/safety/backup.py:325) while docs/specs/safety-net.md:47 says mode 0700, so a future journal.jsonl at the root would be world-readable; and the compose mount hardcodes ${HOME}/.local/share/cortex, so a custom SAFETY_STORE_DIR makes the host CLI and the container use different stores, contrary to the spec's 'same directory' sentence; the one-shot's ${UID:-1000} fallback is 1000 because bash does not export UID/GID by default, so a host user with another UID must set them in .env or the init chowns the store away from the host CLI.

Both new commands follow the typer/--db-url/asyncio.run shape, but they load the composed root settings unconditionally (cli.py:341 and cli.py:383). The root requires LLM_API_KEY (src/cortex/config/models.py:57), so with no LLM key the command dies in settings validation before any backup work. Reproduced from an empty CWD: python -c 'from cortex.cli import cli; cli()' backup:create --db-url ... --out ... -> exit 1, LLMSettings.api_key Field required. The cited traces:cleanup/rules:list load settings only for values not supplied by flags. Backup does need safety.backup_retention, so settings are not avoidable entirely, but the unrelated LLM secret is; consider constructing the safety/database slices directly or making the LLM key optional for non-LLM commands. The CLI tests monkeypatch get_settings and do not catch this.

SafetySettings subclasses CortexSettings, is composed on Settings (models.py:64), is listed in loader._SETTINGS_SECTIONS, has config.yaml and .env.example sections, expands ~ before Path validation, validates backup_retention ge=0, and tests/settings_env.py registers SAFETY_ for the ambient-env guard. tests/config/test_safety.py covers defaults, env overrides, YAML, tilde, and 0/negative retention; all in the 55-passed run.

Pending versions are computed before applying (line 70), the dump is taken only when pending and backup_on_migration (line 72), and _pre_migration_backup raises RuntimeError when require_backup_before_migration is true (line 108) or logs and continues otherwise (line 111); main.py:135 passes settings. tests/unit/test_migrations_backup.py covers no-pending/no-files/no-dump, backup-on-false, fail-closed-before-insert, continue-when-not-required, and constructor failure. Advisory: the test proves a dump happened, not that it happened before the apply loop; a reorder mutant would stay green.

Host pg_dump/pg_restore is preferred; the Docker fallback is limited to local hosts and fails loudly for remote hosts, a missing docker binary, or a missing compose file; the password is only in the environment (docker forwards -e PGPASSWORD by name), the URL is sanitized, the dump is written to a same-directory temp file, chmod 0600 and os.replace'd, and _prune skips the just-created path. Tests: TestHostTransport, TestDockerTransport, TestTransportSelection, TestRetention; all in the 55-passed run. Advisories: the fallback's 'local compose' test is hostname-only (_LOCAL_HOSTS) and ignores port/database, so a local non-compose Postgres on localhost:5432 could be dumped from the compose service instead; the Docker dump buffers the whole archive in memory (target.write_bytes(stdout)); two concurrent creates in the same second can pick the same base name and os.replace over each other.

Resolved for the fatal regression: 823583a removes the cortex service's user: line, so the container is root again and the mosquitto passwd write works; I verified docker run --rm -u 0 --entrypoint sh eclipse-mosquitto:2 -c 'touch /mosquitto/config/passwd.conf' succeeds (the previous UID-1000 run was Permission denied). The one-shot now creates backups/ and snapshots/ and chown -R's the store to the host user; BackupService additionally chowns each new dump to the store directory's uid/gid (backup.py:354/368). I tested the exact init command with busybox on a bind mount: a root-owned 0600 file became 1000:1000 0600 and the host (uid 1000) read it; the root-container _chown logic (stat store, os.chown file, 0600) also produced 1000:1000 0600 and a host-readable file. Non-root is NOT implemented; the delta explicitly defers it to #120, whose body does include the Docker-hygiene companion (non-root USER, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, ro rootfs) - a documented scope change, not a functional regression. Residual advisories are recorded in the STD-1-residual row.

The autovacuum/background-worker false positive is fixed by AND backend_type = 'client backend'. Tests: test_refuses_while_the_database_is_in_use now asserts the filter string; the 58-test feature run and 1432-test canonical run pass. Live check I ran on pgvector/pgvector:pg16 with the exact new query: 0 with only the checking session, 1 with a second pg_sleep session. Advisory: the filter narrows the documented 'any connection' to client backends; logical replication apply workers, pg_cron, walsenders and other background writers are now ignored, so a background writer could be missed. If the spec's wording is literal, exclude only autovacuum workers instead.

The dump-before-apply ordering caveat is resolved by test_dump_happens_before_the_first_migration_is_applied (tests/unit/test_migrations_backup.py:198), which appends backup/execute events and asserts EVENTS.index('backup') < EVENTS.index('execute:SELECT 2;'); a reorder mutant would fail it. Ran uv run pytest tests/safety tests/unit/test_migrations_backup.py tests/unit/test_cli_backup.py tests/config/test_safety.py -q -> 58 passed; canonical suite -> 1432 passed, 28 skipped. Remaining (unchanged) AC-6 advisories: the transport tests use fakes, so no real pg_dump/pg_restore is executed, and the CLI tests monkeypatch get_settings so the LLM_API_KEY prerequisite is untested.

Residual ownership/host-readability edges after the fix, none fatal on the Linux/uid-1000 default: (1) the one-shot uses ${UID:-1000}/${GID:-1000}; bash does not export UID/GID, so on a non-1000 host the store and dumps go to 1000 and the host CLI cannot read them unless UID/GID are set in .env; .env.example:44 still says UID/GID are 'used by the compose cortex service' after the user: revert, so the comment is stale. (2) _chown_to_store_owner is best-effort: on NFS root-squash, Docker Desktop, a cap-drop CHOWN, or a filesystem refusing chown, the dump stays root 0600 and the host CLI cannot read it; the pre-migration dump succeeds with only a warning. (3) the store root is still 0755 (docs/specs/safety-net.md:47 says 0700); the backups dir is chmodded 0700 by _ensure_dir, but snapshots/ and a future root-level journal.jsonl would be world-listable/readable. (4) os.chown is Unix-only: on a Windows host the uncaught AttributeError would fail every backup (the project is Linux/Docker-oriented; no Windows support is documented). (5) chown -R runs on every up over the whole store; busybox does not follow symlinks in my test, so the symlink/TOCTOU risk is limited to the mounted store, and the owner-race window is low risk.
